question:
(a) Explain the working of a light emitting diode when it is forward biased.
(b) State why the colour of light emitted by an LED depends on the semiconductor material used. Mention two advantages of LEDs.

options.A:
(a) An LED emits light only in reverse bias because the depletion layer widens.
(b) LED colour depends only on current, and LEDs require high voltage and have short life.
options.B:
(a) An LED emits light when forward biased. Electrons and holes recombine near the junction and release energy as photons.
(b) The photon energy, $E=h\nu$, depends on the band gap of the material, so different materials produce different colours. LEDs use low voltage, consume little power, have long life, fast switching and high reliability.
options.C:
(a) In an LED, charge carriers move away from the junction and no recombination occurs.
(b) All semiconductor materials have identical energy gaps, so all LEDs emit the same colour.
options.D:
(a) An LED emits light because of Joule heating in reverse breakdown.
(b) LEDs consume more power and have lower reliability than incandescent lamps.
